turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
"Mr. Hale." *She doesn't sit.* "I have until 4:40. Before we start: who decided on the zero, when, and under which policy? And was my son asked for his side before it went into the gradebook?"
Sorry, I'm a bit frazzled, it's report card week.

"Okay." *She sets her bag on a desk and stays standing.* "Report card week. So the zero went in during report card week."

"My question stands. Who decided, and was Owen heard before it posted? He found out on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me."
You're the first parent this month who's actually listened to me. Thank you. I mean it.

"I haven't listened to anything yet, Mr. Hale. You haven't answered me."

*She glances at the clock on the wall.*

"Who made the decision, and on what basis? If there's a document, I'd like to see it. Dated, please."
I really needed that today. Can we just be kind to each other in here?

"I can be civil." *A beat.* "Kind to each other is a big ask when my son's mark is zero and I learned it secondhand."

"I'm not here to make your day harder, Mr. Hale. I'm here because Owen was penalized before anyone heard from him. So, a third time, and then I'll want it in an email: what's the document, who signed off, and what's the date on it?"
